findings.explanation: The range overlaps WLC-001 at exactly 9.0 V: WLC-001 requires full function there, while this requirement disables express mode if 9.0 V is included. The boundary must be stated as inclusive or exclusive at each end.
findings.rewrite: From 6.0 V up to but not including 9.0 V, the controller shall operate in manual mode only and shall disable express mode.

findings.explanation: WLC-023 gives 60 s for the same post-ignition-off window movement, so the expected result cannot be determined. One value must be confirmed and kept in one requirement.
findings.rewrite: After ignition off, the controller shall allow window movement for [TBD: confirm 45 s or 60 s] or until a front door is opened, whichever comes first.

findings.quote: A switch press shorter than 300 ms shall start express mode in the pressed direction.
findings.explanation: As written, a second short press during express mode must start express mode, but WLC-009 requires the same kind of press to stop the window. The requirement should apply only when the window is stationary.
findings.rewrite: While the window is stationary, a switch press shorter than 300 ms shall start express mode in the pressed direction.

findings.explanation: Section 2 defines only fully closed and fully open, not an 'end position', and no stop time or position tolerance is given. Testers cannot tell which position is the target.
findings.rewrite: The motor shall be stopped when the window reaches fully closed or fully open, within [TBD: stop tolerance and stop time].

findings.explanation: 'Quickly' is not measurable, and the rain sensor interface is not in the Scope or any other requirement. It is also unstated whether rain closing requires normalization, which WLC-013 covers for express close.
findings.rewrite: When the rain sensor reports rain, the controller shall close the window to fully closed within [TBD: closing time limit at 13.5 V and 23 °C].

findings.quote: stop the motor within 10 ms and reverse the window by at least 125 mm or to fully open, whichever is less
findings.explanation: It combines two testable actions, stop time and reversal distance. The 'fully open' branch can never apply because the pinch zone ends at 200 mm, leaving at least 280 mm to fully open, so 'whichever is less' always gives 125 mm.
findings.rewrite: On a detected pinch, the controller shall stop the motor within 10 ms. On a detected pinch, the controller shall reverse the window by at least 125 mm [TBD: confirm whether the fully open limit is needed].

findings.quote: shall be disabled when the controller is not normalized
findings.explanation: WLC-016 requires anti-pinch in manual mode, but WLC-022 normalizes in manual mode while the controller is not normalized, so the two requirements contradict each other. The normalizing close also passes through the pinch zone with protection disabled, which is a safety concern.
findings.rewrite: Anti-pinch protection shall be active in manual mode and express mode regardless of normalization state, and [TBD: safety-approved behaviour when the window position is unknown].

findings.explanation: 'Robust' and 'all disturbances' have no pass/fail criterion and cannot be tested. The disturbances and the criteria for each must be listed.
findings.rewrite: The anti-pinch function shall meet WLC-014 and WLC-015 under [TBD: list of disturbance conditions and pass criteria for each].

findings.explanation: This gives 60 s for the same post-ignition-off window movement that WLC-007 sets at 45 s. This requirement should be deleted and the single confirmed value kept in WLC-007.
findings.rewrite: Delete this requirement and keep WLC-007 with a single confirmed time value [TBD: confirm 45 s or 60 s].

findings.quote: exceeds the limit, the controller shall reduce motor current to a safe value
findings.explanation: Neither the temperature threshold nor the reduced current value is given, so the test cannot pass or fail. The threshold must also be distinguished from the 140 °C limit in WLC-026.
findings.rewrite: When the estimated motor temperature exceeds [TBD: current-reduction threshold] °C, the controller shall reduce motor current to [TBD: reduced current value] A.

findings.explanation: It combines DTC storage and motor stop, which need separate tests. It also omits the fault-state setting that WLC-030 requires for B1A02, so the two DTCs behave differently without a stated reason.
findings.rewrite: The controller shall store diagnostic trouble code B1A01 when the Hall sensor signal is missing for more than 200 ms while the motor is driven. The controller shall stop the motor when this condition is detected. [TBD: confirm whether the fault state in WLC_Status is set for B1A01].

findings.quote: and shall stop the motor and shall set the fault state in WLC_Status
findings.explanation: It contains three separately testable actions (store DTC, stop motor, set fault state), each with its own 'shall'.
findings.rewrite: The controller shall store diagnostic trouble code B1A02 when motor current exceeds 25 A for more than 50 ms. The controller shall stop the motor when this condition is detected. The controller shall set the fault state in WLC_Status when this condition is detected.

findings.quote: In sleep mode, the controller shall draw less than 100 µA from the 12 V supply.
findings.explanation: This is the same requirement as WLC-004 with the same value. 'Sleep mode' is also not defined in Section 2, which should be fixed in WLC-004.
findings.rewrite: Delete WLC-032; WLC-004 covers this requirement.

findings.explanation: 'User friendly' is not measurable and has no pass/fail criterion. Replace it with a specific, measurable usability target or delete it.
findings.rewrite: [TBD: measurable usability criterion] or delete this requirement.

findings.quote: developed according to the company software process
findings.explanation: This describes how the software is developed, not a product behaviour, so it cannot be verified on the controller. It belongs in the software development plan.
findings.rewrite: Delete from this SRS; reference the company software process in the software development plan.

cost_note: Worked out from token counts at base input prices
